metadata.title: Remnix Agent
metadata.persona: Revan C (first person, synthetic Kokoro voice)
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Student pitch on the show-tell chassis: opens on the hesitant writer, then a plain-language beat instead of the terms card, no verdict card, and no Claude.ai Your Turn composer (the film shows no Claude interface or response). Outro is the student's own card, narrated as themselves.
metadata.audience: hiring managers and engineers at fintech and crypto companies; INFO 7375 reviewers
metadata.source_doc: PROJECT-BRIEF.md (2026-10-14); Money Map, https://mit-dci.github.io/payments-dashboard/ (viewed and screenshotted 2026-10-14); World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide methodology and US→Mexico corridor pages (viewed 2026-10-14); Wise and Monito checks by Revan (2026-10-14)

beats.narration_text: Hola. I'm Revan, a graduate student at Northeastern. This film pitches a project that doesn't exist yet, for people sending money to family in Mexico. The obvious question is which way is cheapest. Remnix will also answer why.

show.event: 'is cheapest' → 'is cheapest and why' on the spoken correction

props.text:
Which way to send $500
to Mexico is cheapest?
props.brandLabel: Synthetic voice (Kokoro) · written with Claude, reviewed by Revan

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive 'cheapest' question and corrects it to 'cheapest and why'.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: When you send money home to Mexico, part of it disappears in fees and the exchange rate. Remnix will be like a calculator that shows its work: you ask what it costs, and it shows every number and where it came from.

shot.visual_intent: A stack of bills labelled '$500'; two bills slide off into a small tray labelled 'fees'; then a receipt page appears and its lines write in (the calculator showing its work).
shot.motion_claim: A stack of bills labelled '$500'; two bills slide off into a small tray labelled 'fees'; then a receipt page appears and its lines write in (the calculator showing its work).

beats.narration_text: First, what's real. As a software engineer co-op at the MIT Digital Currency Initiative, I built Money Map, a public dashboard that's live today. It compares banks, apps, transfer services and stablecoins for sending dollars to Mexico.

shot.visual_intent: The real Money Map screenshot (cropped header + map) slides onto the stage inside an ink frame; a tag beside it lands: 'real screenshot · 2026-10-14'.
shot.motion_claim: The real Money Map screenshot (cropped header + map) slides onto the stage inside an ink frame; a tag beside it lands: 'real screenshot · 2026-10-14'.

beats.narration_text: Money Map is a dashboard: you pick filters and read numbers. So I will build Remnix, an agent you can ask in plain words, like: why is Wise cheaper than my bank? It will answer with Money Map's data, showing the math and the source behind every number. None of it exists yet.

shot.visual_intent: A sealed kraft crate drops onto the stage, drawn in dashed outline (not built); labels 'Remnix' and 'proposed' sit beside it.
shot.motion_claim: A sealed kraft crate drops onto the stage, drawn in dashed outline (not built); labels 'Remnix' and 'proposed' sit beside it.

beats.narration_text: It will be a public GitHub repo. A Postgres database will hold three tables: quotes, exchange rates and snapshots, each row stamped with its source and time. A Fast API endpoint, POST slash ask, will take the question.

shot.visual_intent: Database drawers with three table labels beside them (quotes, fx_rates, snapshots); then a server tower labelled 'POST /ask' appears and a cable draws from it to the drawers.
shot.motion_claim: Database drawers with three table labels beside them (quotes, fx_rates, snapshots); then a server tower labelled 'POST /ask' appears and a cable draws from it to the drawers.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Then Claude will pick one of two tools: get quotes, which reads prices from the database, or compute cost, which does the math in Python, not in the language model. The answer will come back with the row IDs and timestamps it used.

shot.visual_intent: An agent workstation with two tool blocks beside it (get_quotes, compute_cost); the compute_cost tool undocks; an answer page appears with its 'row IDs' label.
shot.motion_claim: An agent workstation with two tool blocks beside it (get_quotes, compute_cost); the compute_cost tool undocks; an answer page appears with its 'row IDs' label.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Its rule will be a prompt contract: no number without a source. This card is a constructed mock-up; its number is real, from my Money Map screenshot: a thousand dollars with Wise cost seven fifty-four.

shot.visual_intent: An answer page with a large hero number '$7.54'; a source tag 'Money Map · Oct 14' clips to its edge; a big 'CONSTRUCTED' label sits beside the page the whole beat.
shot.motion_claim: An answer page with a large hero number '$7.54'; a source tag 'Money Map · Oct 14' clips to its edge; a big 'CONSTRUCTED' label sits beside the page the whole beat.

beats.narration_text: Money Map models a stablecoin sandwich: dollars become a stablecoin, a digital dollar, cross a blockchain, then become pesos. Remnix will show the cost of each layer.

shot.visual_intent: Three slabs stack one at a time (buy, send, sell); a terracotta dot lights on each slab as it lands.
shot.motion_claim: Three slabs stack one at a time (buy, send, sell); a terracotta dot lights on each slab as it lands.

beats.narration_text: I checked three alternatives on October fourteenth. Wise's comparison page and Monito didn't include stablecoin routes, and the World Bank's newest data for this corridor is from August twenty twenty-five. Remnix will include them, every number sourced.

shot.visual_intent: Three comparison trays in a row labelled Wise, Monito, World Bank; the sandwich slab tries each of the first two and doesn't fit; a dated tag drops on the third.
shot.motion_claim: Three comparison trays in a row labelled Wise, Monito, World Bank; the sandwich slab tries each of the first two and doesn't fit; a dated tag drops on the third.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? Hiring managers and engineers at fintech and crypto companies, my target role as a software engineer, plus researchers and policymakers who study remittance costs. In sixty seconds, they'll run one command and trace every number to a database row.

shot.visual_intent: A README page opens; a dark terminal block runs (a terracotta cursor light); an answer page appears and leader lines run from it to one drawer; a '60 s' counter climbs.
shot.motion_claim: A README page opens; a dark terminal block runs (a terracotta cursor light); an answer page appears and leader lines run from it to one drawer; a '60 s' counter climbs.

beats.narration_text: The first piece I'll make run: load Money Map's Mexico data into Postgres and answer one question with sources. You'll know it ran when the total matches Money Map's snapshot, sources printed.

shot.visual_intent: Records drop into the drawers; one answer page and one Money Map page sit side by side with the same number; a check mark draws between them.
shot.motion_claim: Records drop into the drawers; one answer page and one Money Map page sit side by side with the same number; a check mark draws between them.

beats.narration_text: Then twenty known-answer questions: a pie test suite will score them the same way every run, and write each wrong answer, and how it was caught, to a log.

shot.visual_intent: A queue of question cards in a row passes a checkpoint scanner one by one; a hero '20' sits above; one card is pulled aside into an open binder (the wrong-answer log).
shot.motion_claim: A queue of question cards in a row passes a checkpoint scanner one by one; a hero '20' sits above; one card is pulled aside into an open binder (the wrong-answer log).

beats.narration_text: What's out: Remnix will not move money, or tell anyone which provider to choose. It will explain costs, for one corridor only: U S to Mexico.

shot.visual_intent: A parcel rolls toward a permission gate; the barrier drops and stops it; one single arrow 'US → MX' draws beside it.
shot.motion_claim: A parcel rolls toward a permission gate; the barrier drops and stops it; one single arrow 'US → MX' draws beside it.

beats.narration_text: What could sink it? Money Map's prices are live. On October fourteenth, the stablecoin route moved from seven forty-two to eight ninety-nine within about an hour. So known answers go stale. I'll freeze a dated snapshot for testing.

shot.visual_intent: A price page's number ticks up (7.42 → 8.99); then a copy of the page is clamped and dropped into a vault with a date tag; the vault bar locks.
shot.motion_claim: A price page's number ticks up (7.42 → 8.99); then a copy of the page is clamped and dropped into a vault with a date tag; the vault bar locks.

beats.narration_text: What will this prove? Source grounding, tool calling, prompt contracts and evaluation. A reviewer could fairly conclude I can build a small, checked AI tool on real payment data, backed by the test scores and the wrong-answer log.

shot.visual_intent: A review desk: a results page slides onto it (test scores); an evidence binder lands beside it (wrong-answer log).
shot.motion_claim: A review desk: a results page slides onto it (test scores); an evidence binder lands beside it (wrong-answer log).

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. It builds on Money Map and points at the fintech work I want. Cost modeling, dashboards and GitHub Pages I already have; Money Map is the evidence. New to me: source grounding, tool calling, evaluation, Postgres and Fast API.

shot.visual_intent: Two shelves: left 'have' holds three solid blocks next to the Money Map page; right 'new' shows five dashed outlines that draw in one by one.
shot.motion_claim: Two shelves: left 'have' holds three solid blocks next to the Money Map page; right 'new' shows five dashed outlines that draw in one by one.

beats.narration_text: So today, one thing exists: Money Map. Everything else in this film is a plan.
